Fighting.Description: A measure of raw combat ability. Used to determine if the character lands a blow in hand-to-hand combat, evades blunt attacks, and succeeds in multiple combat attacks or other feats involving hand-to-hand combat.

Agility.Description: A measure of dexterity and nimbleness. Used to determine if the character hits with a thrown or aimed weapon, dodges missile attacks, catches objects, handles vehicles, and determines the secondary ability known as Health.

Strength.Description: A measure of physical muscle power. Used to determine damage inflicted in slugfest combat, success and damage in wrestling combat and other maneuvers, destruction of materials, lifting heavy objects, and the secondary ability known as Health.

Endurance.Description: A measure of personal toughness and physical resistance. Used to determine normal moving speed, success in charging attacks, avoiding the effects of disease, poison, and gas, performing actions over a long period of time, resisting effects of Slams, Stuns, and Kill results, and the amount of Health regained by a wounded individual.

Reason.Description: A measure of intelligence and the capacity for logical thought. Used to determine the character's success in building things, understanding unknown technology and languages, and the secondary ability known as Karma.

Intuition.Description: A measure of wisdom, wits, common sense, and battle reflexes. Used to discover clues, determine initiative in combat, detect hidden or dangerous items, resist effects of emotion control powers, spells, and abilities, and the secondary ability known as Karma.

Psyche.Description: A measure of mental strength and willpower. Used to show resistance to mental and will-dominating attacks, resistance to magical attacks, determine initial magical abilities for characters who wield magic, and the secondary ability known as Karma.

Health.Description: Used to determine the amount of physical damage the character can absorb before losing consciousness and potentially dying. Recovered after damage is taken, and regained through normal healing by the Endurance rank number of points per day.

Karma.Description: Used by the hero as a measure of experience, allowing the hero to perform actions that may otherwise be impossible. Gained through performing heroic acts and lost through performing selfish acts. May be spent to modify die rolls, stay alive, build things, use magical abilities, and raise ability ranks through advancement.

Resources.Description: A measure of how wealthy a character is, and how the character may use that wealth. Used to determine if a character can afford a particular item or service.

Popularity.Description: A measure of the character's reputation in their normal environment. Used to determine reactions of large groups of people and neutral NPCs, and to gain favors, information, and equipment from Contacts.

Powers.Description: Super-human abilities possessed by individual heroes and villains. Used to perform actions above and beyond the limits of normal mortals.

Talents.Description: Non-super-human abilities that may be possessed by characters. Used to perform specialized actions at a specific benefit.

Contacts.Description: Represent social, political, and personal friends and allies through whom the character may gain information and equipment. Contacts are considered as Friendly to the character for purposes of determining reactions.

Types.Ability FEAT: Those that rely on one of the seven primary abilities (Fighting, Agility, Strength, Endurance, Reason, Intuition, and Psyche). These FEATs may be raised or lowered by Talents or the existing situation.
Types.Power FEAT: Those that rely on one the hero's individual Powers: a character with Water Control of Amazing checks on the Amazing column to determine success.
Types.Talent FEAT: Those that rely on the hero's Talents, where the Talent modifies a specific ability for FEATs.
Types.Popularity FEAT: Those used in social interaction, and use the Popularity rank, and may be modified by Contacts.
Types.Resource FEAT: Used in connection with the character's Resource rank, and determine if the character can afford a specific item or piece of equipment.

Intensity Rank versus Ability Rank.Three or More Lower: Usually Automatic Success except special circumstances.
Intensity Rank versus Ability Rank.Two or More Greater: May be Impossible.  Resource FEAT aways Impossible

Types.Daily Life: Small actions that usually wil not involve any fighting.
Types.Petty Crime: Petty crime, street crime, and youth gangs These crimes are small stuff in the nature of the universe ,but important to the people involved.
Types.Robbery: Thefts from people, in which lives may be threatened. Muggings and hostage situations for profit are included in this category.
Types.Burglary: Theft of property in which threatening lives is not a prime factor. Break-ins, thefts, and arson all fall into this general category.
Types.Rampage: Widespread destruction without the motivation of profit. Rampages are often (but not always) the province of powerful villains.
Types.Vendetta: A grudge match, the superpowered slugfest at its most basic.
Types.Organized Crime: Can involve any of the lower crimes, with a twist; someone higher up is doing the planning.
Types.Catastrophe: Crimes and actions that threaten the well-being of the city and its people: Alien invasions!...Deadly Plagues!...Widespread fires!
